rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's fifteen builder trees go (corals, two canary date palms and ficus along the back fences, corals 2.9-4.2 m from the house fronts, magnolias and a jacaranda by the seating); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: by the two arbors, the adirondack chair, the open lot corner, and one back yard 12 m from the house.

trees.why: the north-west back yard with the garden arbor (1.1 m off): a magnolia beside it
the south-east yard's garden arbor (1.2 m off): the same
the south-west yard with the adirondack chair (1.8 m off): a jacaranda to sit under
the open lot corner at the south-west, 25 m from the walls: an old ficus
the north back yard, 12 m from the house: the yard's tree
